extracted.intended_audience: companies considering B Corp Certification (founders, sustainability/CSR leaders, legal and impact teams)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for companies seeking B Corp Certification, including what is assessed, the certification process (B Impact self-assessment and third‑party verification), and the expectations for transparency, accountability, and substantiated sustainability claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meet standards for social, environmental, and governance performance, transparency, and accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: B Corp Certification verifies a company is meeting standards for social and environmental performance, transparency, and accountability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phrase used on the page: 'a company verified as meeting standards for social and environmental performance, transparency, and accountability.' This is the overarching requirement that certification demonstrates to stakeholders (customers, employees, investors) the company's commitment to responsible business practices that benefit people and the planet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification against the B Lab Standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies are certified against the B Lab Standards, a globally recognized framework that assesses a company's social and environmental impact across key areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Standards cover key areas 'from climate action to human rights.' The page emphasizes that the B Lab Standards are the credible framework used to evaluate impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent third‑party audit and verification (ISO 17021-1 based)
rubrics_metrics.description: The certification process is independently audited and verified by a third party, based on ISO 17021-1 requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit procedural requirement: third‑party audit/verification per ISO 17021-1. This establishes rigour and credibility for the certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register on B Impact and complete a self‑assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin by signing up to B Impact and completing a free self-assessment to measure your company's current impact performance against the B Lab Standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page describes this as a 'deep dive' on company impact: 'beginning your self-assessment. This is a deep dive on your company’s impact, measuring your current performance against the B Lab Standards.' The self‑assessment is the entry point to certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certify against the current Standards version (V2.1 from 2026)
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies applying from 2026 will certify against V2.1 of the B Lab Standards, which establishes a stronger, more transparent foundation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Versioning is material: the page notes the April 2025 update and that applicants from 2026 must follow V2.1. Organizations must ensure they meet the requirements of the applicable Standards version when applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrated impact management across social, environmental, and governance practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards and assessment expect integrated management of impact spanning social, environmental, and governance business practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page highlights 'Integrated impact management' and that the standards 'span social, environmental, and governance business practices, from climate action to human rights.' This implies expectation of systemic/integrated policies and processes rather than isolated initiatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make substantiated claims to avoid greenwashing and comply with regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: B Corp Certification enables companies to make substantiated sustainability claims, reducing risk of greenwashing and helping comply with sustainability‑related regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance/expectation: certified companies should be able to back up claims — the certification serves as verification that supports legitimate marketing and regulatory compliance ('Make substantiated claims, reduce the risk of greenwashing, and comply with sustainability-related regulations').

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate transparency and accountability to stakeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: Certification signals transparency and accountability to customers, employees, and investors about a company's commitment to responsible practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page frames transparency and accountability both as evaluation dimensions and as communication signals to external stakeholders. The certification process and third‑party verification support those signals.
